_comment: What the nightly update check (home/dot_local/bin/update-check, #550) watches. One entry per flake input, one rolling PR per entry (branch update/<input>). follow = branch: the input tracks a branch and `nix flake update <input>` moves it. follow = release: flake.nix pins a tag or a commit, and the check moves the pin to the newest stable GitHub release. versions are flake attribute paths read before and after; notes name the GitHub releases whose bodies go into the PR for the version range. hosts are the closures the gate builds; build names any further flake output it builds (a package no host enables yet). switch is what a switch to the bump restarts, written for Tom. Adding a program is an edit here. The clock is a routine on the substrate floor (substrate T-7); nothing in this repo schedules it. issues watches report upstream releases without changing source pins. Kitty compares complete official stable GitHub versions independently of its fixed source recipe; kernel compares major.minor only and ignores release candidates.

inputs.name: llm-agents
inputs.switch: Home Manager only. Running agent sessions keep the binary they started with; the next session starts on the new one. The substrate units find claude and codex through the profile, so their unit text does not change and nothing restarts. dsh is the pkgs/dsh wrapper around llm-agents.dsh; its policy is store --patch overlays, so a bump changes nothing under ~/.dsh, and checks.dsh-config (built above) re-checks the policy against the new release. checks.dsh-plugins (built above) re-runs the herdr profile's plugin tests against the new dsh-tools and boots that profile; its plugins are re-linked under ~/.dsh/profiles/herdr only when Tom next runs `dsh herdr`. checks.dsh-zen (built above) boots the zen profile's OpenCode Zen provider plugin against the new dsh's bundled pi-ai, which is where a bump breaks that plugin first. opencode (pkgs.llm-agents.opencode) is the headless client behind the `zen` wrapper for the Zen free lane, never a harness; a bump changes which client fingerprint Zen sees, so the first `zen` call after the switch is the check.

inputs.name: herdr
inputs.switch: The herdr server keeps X-SwitchMethod=keep-old, so a switch never kills a live PTY. The new server runs only after a deliberate `systemctl --user restart herdr`, and existing clients need a new projector launch.

inputs.name: nixpkgs-fresh
inputs.switch: A new kernel is only staged: it runs after the next reboot, which stays Tom's to name. Chrome on the client updates with `deploy .#client`; the NAS takes this only on a NAS deploy, which is a decision.

issues.name: linux
issues.reason: This is a new stable major.minor series, not a point release. The fleet currently selects its kernel from nixpkgs-fresh. Kernel-series adoption and reboot are explicit daytime decisions; this watcher changes neither.

issues.name: kitty
issues.reason: Kitty is source-pinned in pkgs/kitty-0.50.nix, independently of nixpkgs-fresh. Review this official stable release before changing its version, fetchFromGitHub source hash and Go vendorHash; retain or rebase the procfs patch and run the native terminal/editor gates. The manual source/hash/vendor-hash workflow is documented in https://github.com/mecattaf/dotfiles/blob/main/docs/kitty-updates.md . This watch opens or reuses a review issue only: it never edits the recipe, builds a candidate, advances a pin or deploys.
